title: Social Simulations with Large Language Model Risk Utopian Illusion

bias_targets.methodology: Analyzing multi-agent chatroom simulations across five dimensions (role distribution, semantic similarity, keyword persistence, sentiment, and linguistic patterns) to identify the overarching tendency of LLMs to produce idealized, polite, and conflict-free 'Utopian' behavior.

Classifying LLM-generated social roles into ISCO-08 occupational categories and comparing their distribution against real-world global employment statistics (ILO) and textual corpora frequencies (Google Books Ngrams) to measure the overrepresentation of high-status professions.

Evaluating the emotional tone of LLM-generated conversational utterances using VADER sentiment analysis and measuring the frequency of disagreement and negation terms using LIWC, compared against human conversation datasets.
Extracting keywords and importance weights using KeyBERT to track how strongly topics introduced in early conversation turns dominate and persist throughout the subsequent multi-agent dialogue.
